raw_response.adversarial_critique:
1. Numerical & Specification Conflation Discrepancy: Claude's stored row (`effect_estimate`, `provenance_note`, and `exclusion_from_pooling_reason`) misreports `"SKEW (income/tax-payment skew) coefficient 0.457 in the Three-Class-System provinces (responsiveness 0.175)"`. In Table 3 (PDF p. 10 / journal p. 11) and the accompanying text (PDF p. 9 / journal p. 10), `0.457` (asymptotic `t = 1.98`) is the restricted pooled logit coefficient in Column 4 estimated across ALL FOUR provinces (`"without allowing the influence of SKEW to vary across provinces"`, i.e., pooling Three-Class-System Rhineland and Westphalia together with equal-franchise Hannover and Holstein). In Column 5—the unrestricted model that actually separates the electoral regimes—the `SKEW` coefficient for the Rhineland (Three-Class-System baseline) is `0.948` (asymptotic `t = 2.84`) and `SKEW-WESTPHALIA` is `0.14` (`t = 2.80`), compared with `-0.18` (`t = 2.40`) for `SKEW-HANNOVER` and `-4.85` (`t = 1.36`) for `SKEW-HOLSTEIN`. Moreover, the `+1 SD` predicted-probability responsiveness of `0.175` in Column 6 belongs to Column 5's Rhineland estimate (`0.948`), not Column 4's pooled estimate (`0.457`). Claude also omits the printed asymptotic t-statistics from which SEs can be derived (`0.457 / 1.98 = 0.231`; `0.948 / 2.84 = 0.334`) and leaves `outcome_family = "primary_connection"` in the CSV row in direct contradiction to its own provenance note.

2. SWiM Non-Fit Verdict (`justified_nonfit`): Conditional on S590 remaining in the review, excluding it from Families A, B, and C as a reasoned non-fit is unequivocally justified. Even under the broadened A21 titles for Family A (legal status, tenure, recognition, governance) and Family C (utility ownership, regulation, administrative capacity), pooling S590 would be invalid on three grounds: (a) the estimated regression parameter is the slope of a continuous local income-tax skewness ratio (`SKEW`) rather than a binary or institutional treatment indicator; (b) directionally, a positive sign reflects plutocratic vote-weighting (`Three Class System`) empowering wealthy industrialists over middle-income homeowners to approve capital spending, which is substantively opposite to legal empowerment, tenure recognition, or consumer protection for underserved households; and (c) the dependent variable is a city-level capital investment decision (`building a waterworks`) rather than household service access.

3. Review Scope & Eligibility Consistency (`borderline_flag_for_pi`): S590 exhibits an internal scope tension with CK's `2026-10-13 / 2026-10-14` (`A24/A26/A28`) rulings that warrants PI confirmation. Unlike clearly non-legal exposures excluded in `A24/A28` (e.g., watershed engineering `S1020`, social trust `S1144`), S590 does study a genuine statutory governance rule—19th-century Prussian municipal franchise law (`Gemeindewahlrecht`)—and CK explicitly inspected S590 in `A26` (`2026-10-14`) and retained it as a non-fit. However, CK's own `A26` rationale concedes that `"the outcome is whether a 19th-century Prussian city decided to build waterworks (municipal capital investment...), not household connection, access or service quality"`. Under strict Criterion 4 (`E04`, upstream municipal capital investment rather than household connection, reliability, quality, or affordability—analogous to excluding municipal building permits `S1121`), as well as narrow Criterion 2 (general municipal suffrage law rather than a WASH sector access rule, proxied by fiscal inequality in 1880-1887 Prussia), S590 is borderline and should be flagged for PI consistency review (and at minimum `outcome_family` should not be coded `"primary_connection"`, and `0.457` vs `0.948` must be corrected).
